summary: Moved all of the app's LLM traffic to Router through its one shared Anthropic client, ported research web search to the Responses API, and dropped seed on the summarizer. Embeddings stay on OpenAI.
reviewed: Model tiers, retries, caching structure, spend labels, background jobs and the API surface each call uses.

items.title: Route the shared Anthropic client through Router
items.summary: The one Anthropic client every call uses now sends its traffic to Router.
items.gains: All model traffic on Router: one key, spend per feature, provider choice per request
items.why: Every LLM call goes through src/ai/client.ts; routing that client moves all of them with one change.

evidence.detail: 947 pass, 1 failing as before the change
messages.create and count_tokens returned 200 from Router

items.title: Drop seed on the summarizer
items.summary: Router rejects seed, so the summarizer's requests drop it.
items.gains: The nightly summarizer moves to Router
items.loses: Runs are no longer reproducible with a fixed seed
items.why: seed is only used in a debug path.

items.title: Port web search to the Responses API
items.summary: The research agent's web search moves from Anthropic server tools to Router's Responses web search.
items.gains: Web search works through Router on any catalog model
items.loses: Citation format changes; the renderer was updated to match
items.why: Router served Anthropic's tool only on Sonnet 5; the agent runs on Haiku.

evidence.detail: citation tests updated by new tests, existing ones unchanged

items.title: Embeddings stay on OpenAI
items.summary: Router has no embeddings endpoint, so the three embedding calls stay where they are.

items.title: Users' own OpenAI keys
items.summary: Some users bring their own OpenAI key; routing those calls would bill them to your Router key.
items.why: Product decision, not a technical one.

items.title: Classifier on Haiku 5.5
items.summary: The classifier tier moves from claude-haiku-4-5 to claude-haiku-5-5.
items.gains: -90% list price on every classifier call
items.loses: A different model answers: classification may differ
items.why: Short, well-specified outputs; the newer Haiku is far cheaper.

evidence.detail: 10 sample emails: same label on 9, 1 differs (shown below)

items.title: Composer on Opus 5.5
items.summary: The composer tier moves from claude-opus-5 to claude-opus-5-5.
items.loses: A different model writes the replies
items.why: Same family, newer, cheaper; the prompt-caching floor is the same.

items.title: Spend tags per stage
items.summary: Each request carries the pipeline stage as its feature label.
items.why: The app already passes a stage to complete().

items.title: Fallback to GPT-5.4 mini on outages
items.summary: Reply calls fail over to another vendor's model when Anthropic is down.
items.gains: Replies keep going out during an Anthropic outage
items.loses: A different vendor answers those requests

items.title: Flex for the reminder digests
items.summary: The nightly reminder digest runs on Flex.
items.loses: Up to a minute slower; nobody waits

items.title: Cache-friendly system prompt
items.summary: The composer's fixed instructions move ahead of the per-email context.
items.gains: More cache hits on the composer
items.price: cached reads at a tenth of the price
items.why: The fixed prefix was split by per-email text.

items.title: Consolidate retry policy into Router
items.summary: Per-tier retries move to Router fallbacks.

items.title: Flex needs the Responses API
items.summary: Flex, fallbacks and cache keys apply to Responses-style calls; this app uses /v1/messages.
items.why: Moving the reply path to Responses would unlock them; a bigger change, left for you to decide.
